summary: Backend-only testing of NexoraOS. Ran 28 pytest cases against public preview URL covering signup+OTP, login, /me, forgot/reset, categories/products/tables/customers/inventory CRUD, stock transactions (in/out/adjust), order creation with totals+table+customer effects, sequential order_no per cafe, order status flow freeing tables, tenant isolation between two cafes (Owner A vs Owner B), dashboard, reports, staff RBAC (owner-only create, cashier/kitchen 403 on writes), Razorpay create-order for monthly/yearly and non-owner 403, and PATCH /api/cafe. All 28 tests PASS.

minor.issue: Does not implement brute-force lockout or sha256 token_hash storage (raw 6-digit OTP stored in Mongo). Acceptable per current spec (OTP-based) but flagged from the playbook checklist.
Does not clear a brute-force lockout counter (there is none). Same context as above.
Stateless JWT logout returns {message: 'Logged out'} but does not blacklist token; server-side logout is a no-op. Cookie-based httpOnly session is not used (JWT in Authorization header only).
update_order_status does not scope table update by cafe_id when freeing table (uses only table_id). Low risk because table_ids are UUIDs, but should filter by cafe_id for defense in depth.
inventory update on stock txn does not filter by cafe_id (uses only item_id). Same low-risk pattern; recommend adding cafe_id filter.

action_items: Optional: scope table/inventory update writes by cafe_id in create_order/update_order_status/stock_txn for defense-in-depth (currently filters only by resource id).
Optional: remove dev-mode OTP log line before production (server.py line 130 logs OTP in plaintext).

Playbook divergences (informational): app uses stateless JWT in Authorization header (not httpOnly cookie), no brute-force lockout, no sha256 token_hash — these are intentional per current OTP-based auth design but do not match the generic auth playbook.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 743 lines; consider splitting into routers per resource (auth, orders, menu, staff, subscription).
OTP is logged to backend logs in plaintext (line 130). Remove before production.
verify_otp expiry check on line 203 uses a confusing single-line conditional that is hard to read; simplify.
PATCH /orders/{oid} table free logic does not filter table update by cafe_id.
POST /inventory/stock: db.inventory.update_one uses only {'id': item_id} without cafe_id.
CORS allow_origins defaults to '*' with allow_credentials=True — invalid combo per browsers; fine for API-only clients but should tighten in prod.
No pagination on list endpoints (uses .to_list(2000/5000)); will break at scale.
Trial subscription hardcoded to 14 days — acceptable but consider config.
test_credentials: Dynamically generated per test run: TEST_ownerA_<hex>@example.com and TEST_ownerB_<hex>@example.com with password 'Password123!'. OTPs read directly from MongoDB db.otps collection.
seed_data_creation: No manual seed data. Tests create fresh owners/cafes/categories/products/tables/customers/inventory/orders/staff on each run, all prefixed TEST_.
context_for_next_testing_agent: backend_test.py uses pymongo directly to fetch OTPs from db.otps for signup/reset flows. All resources are cafe-scoped by JWT cafe_id claim. Order numbers start at 1001 per cafe and increment. Trial subscription auto-created on signup. Razorpay live keys are configured; only create-order is tested (verify requires real signature). Tenant isolation verified by cross-checking Owner A's cafe_id absent from Owner B's lists and vice versa. TEST_ prefix used throughout for future cleanup.
